_comment: Directional energy-efficiency (performance-per-watt) multipliers for general-purpose instance FAMILIES, used to suggest a greener same-size family in the same region. The carbon mechanism is real: newer process nodes and ARM (Graviton-class) cores do the same work on less energy. 'relative_energy' is the energy drawn to deliver a fixed amount of work, normalised so a modern x86 generation = 1.00; LOWER is greener. These are ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE, directional figures consistent with public vendor/analyst claims (e.g. AWS Graviton ~60% less energy for the same performance; each x86 generation ~10-20% better perf/watt). NOT measured for your workload. Replace with cited, benchmarked values before any non-directional use.
_source: Directional: AWS Graviton energy claims; Intel/AMD generational perf-per-watt disclosures; SPECpower-style public results. Normalised and rounded by GreenPick. Do not cite as measured.
_relative_energy_note: relative_energy LOWER = greener (less energy for the same work). arch 'arm' families are the biggest honest win.

_general_purpose_generations.notes: ARM; AWS claims large energy reduction for same work.
